mainEntity.name: What is an in-law suite and what does it include?

acceptedAnswer.text: An in-law suite is a self-contained living area on a residential property designed for family members, such as aging parents or adult children. These spaces typically include a bedroom, full bathroom, living space, and often a kitchenette or full kitchen. Depending on your home and budget, an in-law suite can be built as a brand-new room addition, converted from an existing garage, or constructed as a separate detached accessory dwelling unit (ADU). Determining whether the suite connects directly to the main interior or maintains a completely separate exterior entrance depends on how much daily privacy and household autonomy your family requires.
acceptedAnswer.description: An in-law suite is a private living space on a home's property featuring a bedroom, bathroom, living area, and sometimes a kitchen, built for aging relatives or guests.
